turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't make myself go near the front windows at work anymore. Or even that part of the street, honestly. turns.doctor_question: Is there something specific that you're afraid of when you think about being near the front windows at work?
turns.patient_response: Well, yeah. A little while ago, a car crashed right through the front of the store while I was working. Now, the crash just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. It just feels like it's happening right in front of me again.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient describes intrusive, involuntary memories and vivid flashback-like sensory experiences of the car crash popping into their head and feeling as though it is happening all over again.

turns.doctor_question: Are there any other situations or places that you're avoiding because of the car crash?

symptom_reasoning.S070: The patient confirms avoiding the specific spot at work where the traumatic car crash occurred.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever have the memory of the car crash popping into your head when you're not near the store or thinking about work?

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing these memories and fears about the car crash at work?
turns.patient_response: It's been about two weeks now. Basically ever since it happened... it was during my overnight shift when the car actually crashed through the window. So, yeah, it's been going on for the last two weeks.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having trouble sleeping since the car crash happened?
turns.patient_response: No, my sleep has been fine, honestly. I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. It's just... normal.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been startled more easily since the car crash happened?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. Um, if a delivery cart bangs in the back, or a car honks outside... or even if someone just comes up behind me, I jump really hard. Like, my whole body just jerks. And then my heart just keeps racing for a while afterward.

symptom_reasoning.S080: The patient confirms experiencing an exaggerated startle response, describing full-body jerks and prolonged heart racing in reaction to everyday sudden noises or people approaching.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding talking or thinking about the car crash?

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself losing interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still like doing the same things I usually do. Like, I still enjoy hanging out with my friends and watching my regular shows. So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in anything.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies any loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, noting they still enjoy seeing friends and watching their regular shows.

turns.doctor_question: Has your difficulty with being near the front windows at work caused any problems in your relationships with coworkers or supervisors?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it kind of has. Um, the other day I actually had to leave right in the middle of a window reset because I just couldn't finish the work. I had to walk away from it. symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient describes having to leave and walk away in the middle of a window reset at work due to difficulty being near the storefront, indicating active avoidance and functional impairment related to the feared situation.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not in a situation that would normally be considered dangerous?

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulties in your personal relationships or daily life outside of work due to your feelings or reactions to the car crash?

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel guilty about what happened with the car crash at work?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't feel guilty. Um, I mean, I was just inside working when it happened. I didn't have anything to do with the car actually crashing into the building, you know? turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling anxious or distressed even when you're not thinking about the car crash or near the front windows at work?

symptom_reasoning.S074: The patient explicitly denies a persistent negative emotional state, stating they feel pretty normal outside of work and are not sitting around feeling anxious or upset without trigger cues.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding other things or activities at work besides being near the front windows?

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding the store altogether on your days off or when you're not working?

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a day where you didn't think about the car crash at all?

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel a strong physical reaction, like your heart racing or sweating, when you think about the car crash or see something that reminds you of it?
